2027-06-18.title: Friday of the Eleventh Week in Ordinary Time
readings: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness
From all their afflictions God will deliver the just
Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also
2027-06-18.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 11 (Year I). The psalm is given in NRSV numbering (Lectionary 34:2–3, 4–5, 6–7 = NRSV 34:1–2, 3–4, 5–6). Liturgical colour: green.
2027-06-18.verse: For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
theo: St Paul's rivals in Corinth boasted of their pedigree, their visions and their eloquence. Paul, who hates boasting, decides to answer them in their own language, but he warns that he is “speaking as a fool.” First, his roots: “Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.” Paul never stopped being proud of his Jewish people. Then, “Are they ministers of Christ? I am talking like a madman, I am a better one.” But instead of listing successes, he lists sufferings: “far greater labors, far more imprisonments, with countless floggings, and often near death.” He received the synagogue's punishment of “forty lashes minus one” five times (Deuteronomy 25:3), a discipline he accepted because he remained a member of the synagogue and went on preaching Christ in it; it is no charge against the Jewish people, among whom Paul counted himself. He was beaten with rods by Roman magistrates three times, stoned once, shipwrecked three times, “adrift at sea” for a night and a day; he faced danger from rivers, bandits, his own people and Gentiles, in city and wilderness and sea; he knew “toil and hardship,” sleepless nights, hunger and thirst, “cold and naked.” And above all, “I am under daily pressure because of my anxiety for all the churches.” This is the heart of a true pastor: “Who is weak, and I am not weak?” Then the surprising conclusion: “If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.” Paul's glory is not his strength but the power of Christ shining through his weakness. The Psalm is the prayer of such a man: “This poor soul cried, and was heard by the Lord, and was saved from every trouble.”

In the Gospel Jesus continues the Sermon on the Mount with two short sayings. The first is about treasure: “Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust consume and where thieves break in and steal.” In the ancient world wealth was kept in fine clothes, which moths eat, and in coins and metals, which rust and which thieves dig through mud walls to steal. Everything earthly passes. “But store up for yourselves treasures in heaven,” which nothing can destroy: love, mercy, faith, the good done for the poor. Then comes the line that unlocks the whole passage: “For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.” Our heart follows what we treasure. The second saying is about the eye: “The eye is the lamp of the body. So, if your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light.” The Greek word for healthy, haplous, also means single, undivided, generous; and in Jewish speech an “evil eye” meant a greedy, stingy heart. An eye fixed on God and generous to others fills the whole life with light; an eye fixed on possessions darkens everything. In this month of June, dedicated by popular devotion to the Sacred Heart of Jesus, today's Gospel invites a simple question: where is my heart? The heart of Jesus has only one treasure: the Father's will and our salvation. To love his Heart is to let our hearts be drawn to the same treasure.
outline: Ask: if a thief broke into my house tonight, what would I most fear to lose? And what can no thief ever take?
Paul's sufferings and his anxiety for all the churches; Christ's power in weakness.
Moth, rust and thieves; the riches that last.
Point 3 · The lamp of the body
A healthy, generous eye fills life with light; where is my heart?
“Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.”
live: Pray for all the churches (2 Corinthians 11:28)
Share Paul's anxiety for the churches: pray today for your parish priest, your bishop, and a persecuted Christian community.
Give away today one thing you are too attached to, or spend one hour of your day on someone who cannot repay you.
2027-06-18.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, your apostle Paul boasted only of his weakness, so that your power might dwell in him. Strengthen all who labour and suffer for your Church, and give our pastors a heart full of care for all the churches. Lord, you have taught us that where our treasure is, there our heart will be also: deliver us from greed for what moth and rust consume, make our eye healthy and generous, and draw our hearts to your own Sacred Heart, where our true treasure is. Amen.
altar: The greatest treasure on earth is on the altar: the Body and Blood of Christ, the pledge of the treasure of heaven. Here is the Heart that was pierced for us, and here our hearts learn where to rest. Every Communion is a moment to move our treasure from earth to heaven.

quick: Paul, speaking “as a fool,” lists not his successes but his sufferings: beatings, shipwrecks, dangers, hunger, and his daily anxiety for all the churches.
He concludes that if he must boast, he will boast of his weakness.
Jesus: store up treasures in heaven, not on earth, for where your treasure is, there your heart will be; the eye is the lamp of the body.
2027-06-18.action: Give away one thing you are attached to, or give one hour to someone in need.
2027-06-18.question: Where is my treasure, and so where is my heart?

family.explain: Jesus says: do not spend your life collecting things that get old, break or are stolen, like toys, phones and money. Collect treasures in heaven: kindness, prayer, sharing, forgiveness. Nobody can steal these! And he says: where your treasure is, your heart will be. If we love Jesus most, our heart will be with him.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries and pastors who suffer for the Church, and for the poor who have no treasure on earth.
family.ask: Ask: “What is the most precious thing in our house? What is the most precious thing in heaven for us?”

illus: An elderly widow in Changanassery kept a small steel box under her bed. When she died, her children opened it, expecting to find gold. Inside they found her wedding ring, a rosary worn smooth, a bundle of letters, and a list in her handwriting: the names of every poor child whose school fees she had paid over forty years, with the year each one finished school. There were sixty-three names. Her grandson, a young engineer, read the list twice and then said quietly: so this is where her heart was. Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also. (An illustrative story.)

pm.open: Lord, from all their afflictions you deliver the just. Draw our hearts to the treasure that does not pass away. Amen.
share: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness (2 Corinthians 11:30). Can I accept my weakness as a place for Christ's power?
I am under daily pressure because of my anxiety for all the churches (2 Corinthians 11:28). Do I carry the Church in my prayer?
Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also (Matthew 6:21). What does my use of time and money say about my heart?
pm.resp: From all their afflictions God will deliver the just.
interc: For the Pope, bishops and priests, who carry the daily care of all the churches.
For missionaries and Christians who suffer hunger, danger and persecution for the Gospel.
For those enslaved by greed and by the love of money.
For the poor, that the Church may share her treasure with them.
For our group, that our hearts may rest in the Sacred Heart of Jesus.
pm.close: Father, your Son's Heart has only one treasure, your will and our salvation. Make our hearts like his. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul's rivals boasted of their gifts and successes. Paul answers them with a list of his sufferings: beatings, imprisonments, shipwrecks, dangers, hunger, cold. And then he adds: besides other things, I am under daily pressure because of my anxiety for all the churches (2 Corinthians 11:28). This is the heart of a true shepherd. Let us remember today our priests and bishops, who carry so many burdens we do not see.

And Paul ends with words that turn the world upside down: if I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness (2 Corinthians 11:30). The world admires the strong, the rich, the successful. Paul says: my glory is my weakness, because there the power of Christ is seen. When we are weak, sick, poor or tired, God is not far from us. He is closest.

In the Gospel Jesus says: do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust consume and where thieves break in and steal (Matthew 6:19). We all know how quickly things pass: the new phone is old in a year, the gold can be stolen, the house needs repair. But there is a treasure no thief can take: the love we give, the prayers we pray, the good we do.

Then Jesus says the key word: for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also (Matthew 6:21). In this month of the Sacred Heart, let us ask ourselves: where is my heart? With my money, my property, my worries? Or with Jesus? His Heart was pierced for us; his only treasure is our salvation. Let us give him our hearts today, and our hearts will be full of light. Amen.
kids: Children, what is your favourite treasure? A toy, a bicycle, a game? Jesus says toys get old and break, and things can get lost. But there are treasures that last forever: when you are kind, when you pray, when you share. These go into your treasure box in heaven! And Jesus says: where your treasure is, there your heart will be. Let us keep our hearts with Jesus.

intro: Theme: “Where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.”
The apostle who boasts of weakness, the treasure that lasts, and the eye that fills life with light.

sub: Labours, dangers and daily anxiety for the churches.
q: Thus says the Lord: Do not let the wise boast in their wisdom, do not let the mighty boast in their might, do not let the wealthy boast in their wealth; but let those who boast boast in this, that they understand and know me,
but he said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.” So, I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell in me.
points.apply: Offer to Christ one weakness you are ashamed of, and ask him to show his power there.

sub: Riches that no one can steal.
q: if riches increase, do not set your heart on them.
but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consumes and where thieves do not break in and steal. For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
points.apply: Look at how you spent your money last month, and move one part of it this month to the poor or the Church.

sub: A heart drawn to the Sacred Heart.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
The eye is the lamp of the body. So, if your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light;
points.apply: Each day this week, spend five minutes before the Blessed Sacrament or an image of the Sacred Heart, giving him your heart.

concl: Paul's glory is his weakness, through which the power of Christ shines.
Our heart follows our treasure: let it be in heaven, in the Heart of Jesus, and our whole life will be full of light.
2027-06-18.resolve: This week, give away one thing you are attached to, and give your heart to Jesus each day.
